chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Let those whom your right hands possess, and those who have not yet reached puberty from you, seek permission three times, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you.
And whoever has reached puberty, let him not enter upon his mother, nor his sister, nor his maternal aunt, nor anyone besides that, except by permission.
So do not give permission until they have greeted, and the greeting is obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Let your servant seek permission from you when he has reached puberty during three times of privacy, when he enters any one of them, even if his room is in your house.
And let him seek permission from you after the evening prayer which is called Al-Atamah, and when it is morning, and when you put off your clothes from the midday heat.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only commanded that for privacy, for these are times of inattention and privacy.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times and conditions for seeking permission in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elaborates on the Quranic command for *istidhan* by specifying three distinct times of privacy (*awrat*)—after the night prayer (*'Atamah*), at dawn, and at midday—when family members must seek permission to enter. The hadith emphasizes that greeting (*salam*) is an act of obedience to God and that permission should not be granted until the greeter has been acknowledged, ensuring modesty and preventing surprise encounters during moments of undress or intimacy.
